Skies will be partly cloudy, with a relatively low chance of precipitation at 18 percent. Models suggest that any rainfall will be isolated and confined to the late afternoon or early evening hours. As the sun sets over Maitama and Garki, residents can expect a gentle breeze out of the southeast, blowing at approximately 1 kilometer per hour. This light wind will contribute to a relatively calm night, with temperatures dipping to a low of 22 degrees Celsius.
The high humidity of 97 percent will make the air feel warmer, especially in low-lying flood-prone areas such as those found near the airport road. As the day wears on, the heat index will rise, making it feel more like 26 degrees Celsius. Despite this, the overall weather pattern for the day will be relatively stable, with no significant wind direction shifts or low-pressure systems affecting the area. As the evening approaches, the partly cloudy skies will give way to clearer conditions, allowing for a pleasant night in areas such as Wuse and Gwarinpa. However, my best guess is that the rain chances will increase as the week progresses, with a more significant chance of precipitation on the horizon. The rainfall accumulation range for the day will be relatively low, likely less than 5 millimeters. ### Tuesday A low-pressure system will begin to develop in the region, leading to an increased chance of rainfall at 62 percent. This shift will contribute to a more unstable atmosphere, with a greater likelihood of thunderstorms in the late afternoon or early evening hours.
The atmosphere will be highly saturated, with humidity levels remaining above 90 percent throughout the day. As a result, the heat index will be higher, making it feel warmer than the actual temperature. Areas such as Aso Rock and the National Assembly complex will experience a slightly cooler temperature due to their elevated locations. The rainfall accumulation range for the day will be higher, potentially exceeding 10 millimeters in some areas.
